title: spec-gates policy
description: Declarative gate policy for Spec Kit projects. Consumed by .specify/gates/lib/policy.sh at runtime and validated by /speckit.gates.init and /speckit.gates.upgrade.

_comment.description: Free-form note field. Ignored by the loader. Authored copies may reference this schema URL here.

$schema.description: Optional schema reference for editor tooling.

extends.description: Versioned baseline contract (feature 003). This policy file becomes an overlay on the named baseline: /speckit.gates.sync fetches source@version once, pins it (baseline.lock.json), snapshots it (baseline.json), and materializes the merged effective policy (policy.effective.json) that every boundary enforces. Absent = the contract machinery is fully dormant.

source.description: Anything git accepts as a remote: https/ssh URL, file:// URL, or local path to the baseline repository.

version.description: Tag or commit identifier to pin. Branch names are refused at sync time — a moving pin is not a pin.

file.description: Path of the baseline policy document inside the source repository.

hooks.description: Map of hook name to hook stanza. Hook names are free-form strings matching the name used by gates_policy_get / gates_policy_list callers. gates, gate_timeout_s and test_severity are accepted only under verify-quality.

protected_files.description: Files refused at the agent PreToolUse boundary, on top of the built-in secret/key defaults. At the git boundary a staged match needs a Protected-Change trailer (see git.protected_change_trailer).

extra.description: Additional paths or globs to protect.

git.description: Toggles for the git-boundary hooks (pre-commit / commit-msg).

block_main_commits.description: Refuse direct commits to main/master (override per-commit with GATES_ALLOW_MAIN_COMMIT=1).

conventional_commits.description: Require Conventional Commits subject format in commit-msg.

forbid_ai_isms.description: Reject AI-ism / self-referential phrasing in commit messages and PRs.

protected_change_trailer.description: Let a staged protected_files.extra path through the git boundary only when the commit message carries a 'Protected-Change: <path>' trailer for every staged protected path plus 'Approved-By: <name>' (checked in commit-msg). false restores the unconditional pre-commit refusal, from the commit after the one that turns it off: that commit is judged by HEAD's policy and passes with its trailers. The agent boundary refuses protected edits either way.

block_bulk_staging.description: Refuse bulk staging at the agent boundary: git add -A / --all / . / :/ / *, or a directory argument. Explicit file paths, -u, --renormalize, git commit -a and -p stay allowed. The git boundary cannot tell how the index was filled, so this rule is agent-boundary only.

ai_branding.description: AI-branding rule of git.forbid_ai_isms, applied by commit-msg and the PR validator.

terms.description: Terms refused as whole words, case-insensitive, matched literally. An empty list disables the branding check (the standalone 'Claude' rule stays).

allow_phrases.description: Literal phrases, matched ignoring case, removed from the message before the branding and standalone 'Claude' checks, e.g. a product or branch name that contains a term.

attestation.description: Gate-run evidence settings: attestation records appended per verify.sh run and the pins-based parity gate. Optional; absence means all defaults apply (enabled, 200 records, parity error).

enabled.description: Append an attestation record to .specify/gates/attestations.jsonl on every verify.sh run (and embed it in --json). false also disables the parity gate; canaries are unaffected.

max_records.description: Cap on attestation log lines; the oldest records are dropped once the cap is exceeded.

parity.description: Severity of the synthetic parity gate when a resolved tool version drifts from its lockfile pin: error fails the run, warning reports without failing, off omits the gate.

spec.description: Spec-conformance gate settings: fenced accept blocks in specs/*/tasks.md run as executable acceptance criteria; features whose spec.md Status is Complete are enforced. Optional; absence means all defaults apply (enabled, error, all features, 30s timeout).

enabled.description: Run the spec gate on every verify.sh run. false removes the spec gate entry and the attestation spec object.

severity.description: How enforcement failures (unchecked tasks, failing accept blocks, parse errors) map to the run result: error fails the run, warning reports without failing.

include.description: Feature-directory-name globs eligible for enforcement when marked Complete. Non-matching complete features stay informational.

timeout_s.description: Per-accept-block watchdog seconds; an exceeded budget fails that criterion.

snapshot_exclude.description: Repository-relative path globs of untracked or gitignored files left out of the accept-block read-only check, for files another process writes while blocks run (an editor or plugin cache). A trailing slash names a directory and everything under it ("cache/" equals "cache/**"). A pattern of only *, ? and / would exempt every path and is refused. Tracked files are always checked.

cover.description: A covering script (feature 007): at the boundaries in at, the spec gate runs `<script> <feature> <task-id> <block-file>` from the project root before each accept block; exit 0 with exactly one non-empty line on stdout marks the block covered (not run, reported by name with that line as reason), anything else runs the block. CI is never covered: CI runs the full policy (constitution, Principle III). The script is protected like policy.json at every boundary.

script.description: Project-relative path of the covering script (not absolute, no .. segment); must be a regular file inside the project, or verify.sh refuses the run. Protected at every boundary, whatever protected_files.extra says.

at.description: Boundaries where the script is asked (agent, git). ci is refused: CI runs the full policy (constitution, Principle III).

timeout_s.description: Time limit in seconds for one answer of the script; on timeout its process group is stopped and the block runs.

include.description: Glob patterns selecting files in scope. Consumed by config generators.

exclude.description: Glob patterns excluded from scope. Consumed by config generators.

orchestrator.description: Dispatch style. none = invoke the native tool directly. task = delegate to a Taskfile target. custom = invoke the command in custom_command.

severity.description: How the hook's overall exit code maps to caller-visible severity.

on_missing_runner.description: Deprecated: no gate reads this field, so it has no effect. It is still accepted so existing policies validate; doctor recommends removing it.

on_missing_tests.description: Deprecated: no gate reads this field, so it has no effect. It is still accepted so existing policies validate; doctor recommends removing it.

custom_command.description: Shell command invoked when orchestrator == custom.

gates.description: Project gates (verify-quality only): named commands run after the orchestrator's gates, in key order, each reported as its own gate in the text report, --json and the attestation. The runtime's own gate names are reserved and refused.

gate_timeout_s.description: Time limit in seconds for project gates without their own timeout_s (verify-quality only). A gate over its limit fails and its process group is stopped.

test_severity.description: Severity of the task-test gate under the task orchestrator (verify-quality only). task-lint stays error.

command.description: Run as sh -c "<command>" from the project root, with GATES_BOUNDARY set to agent, git, ci or none. Exit 126 or 127 fails the gate (command not found or not executable).

severity.description: How a non-zero exit maps: error fails the run, warning and info warn. A timeout or a command that cannot start fails whatever the severity.

timeout_s.description: Time limit in seconds; default gate_timeout_s, else 600.

skip_at.description: Earlier boundaries at which this gate does not run, by declaration; each skip is reported by name. ci cannot be named: CI runs the full policy (constitution, Principle III).
